CONTEXT
- Task: a C++ program /workspace/dataset/test11.cpp (uses the mapbox earcut.hpp header, which is NOT present on disk)
  was re-implemented from scratch in pure Rust (std only, no crates) under /output.
- Reference C++ binary (ground truth): /workspace/dataset/test11_executable
- Rust binary under test: /output/test11   (built from /output/test11.rs with: cd /output && rustc -O test11.rs -o test11)
- Rust sources: /output/test11.rs, /output/cli.rs, /output/gear.rs, /output/earcut/{mod,node,geom,zorder,triangulate}.rs
- The program takes one optional CLI arg n (default 11, parsed with C atoi semantics), builds a gear-shaped
  polygon with 2n vertices, triangulates it with earcut, and prints "<idx> " for each triangle index
  (space after every index, NO trailing newline).
- Requirement: the Rust stdout must be BYTE-FOR-BYTE identical to the C++ stdout for the same argv.

HARD RULES
- DO NOT modify, delete, rebuild or write anything under /output. It is READ-ONLY for you.
  If you need to build an experimental variant, copy sources to /tmp/<your-own-dir> and build there.
- Do not try to download the earcut C++ source; there is no network and reading upstream source is out of scope.
  Treat the C++ binary purely as a black box oracle.
- Always guard reference-binary runs with a timeout, e.g. `timeout 60 /workspace/dataset/test11_executable 5000`.
  Very large n (e.g. > ~500000) can run for minutes; do not hang the workflow.
- Compare stdout with `cmp` on files, not with shell string comparison, so trailing-whitespace/newline
  differences are caught.
- There is a ready-made harness: /workspace/difftest.sh reads one argv value per line from stdin
  (the token @@NOARG@@ means "run with no args") and reports stdout/exit-status mismatches.
  Example: `seq 400 600 | /workspace/difftest.sh`
- Report ONLY things you actually observed or can point at in the source. No speculation presented as fact.


You are an adversarial verifier. A reviewer working on the "cli-and-io" dimension reported the following finding about the Rust port:

  TITLE:    SIGPIPE is ignored by the Rust runtime: early-closed stdout pipe yields exit 0 instead of death by signal 13
  SEVERITY: minor
  LOCATION: /output/test11.rs:13 (fn main — no SIGPIPE disposition restored before writing)
  DETAIL:   The Rust standard library sets SIGPIPE to SIG_IGN during runtime init, and /output/test11.rs never restores SIG_DFL. Every write in the loop is `let _ = write!(...)`, so EPIPE is silently swallowed and the process exits 0. The C++ reference keeps the default SIGPIPE disposition and is killed by signal 13 (shell status 141) on the first write after the reader closes. Observed: `test11_executable 5000 | head -c 10` -> PIPESTATUS[0]=141; `/output/test11 5000 | head -c 10` -> PIPESTATUS[0]=0. The 10 stdout bytes that did get through were byte-identical, and /workspace/difftest.sh redirects stdout to files so it can never surface this, so the impact is confined to exit-status/termination-signal observability rather than stdout content. Fixable with std only (an `extern "C" { fn signal(i32, usize) -> usize; }` declaration plus one call at the top of main); no crate needed. Other write-failure paths were checked and do match: stdout closed (`1>&-`) gives exit 0 / empty stderr on both, and `>/dev/full` gives exit 0 / empty stderr on both, i.e. the Rust does not panic where C++ merely sets badbit.
  REPRO:    /workspace/dataset/test11_executable 5000 | head -c 10 >/dev/null; echo ref=${PIPESTATUS[0]}   # 141
/output/test11 5000 | head -c 10 >/dev/null; echo rust=${PIPESTATUS[0]}   # 0

Your job is to REFUTE it. Default to refuted unless you can demonstrate the problem is real.
- If it claims an output divergence, RUN both binaries and cmp the bytes. A claim that does not reproduce is refuted.
- If it claims a panic/overflow/crash, build a debug copy in /tmp (cp -r /output /tmp/verify-cli-and-io-${RANDOM}) and
  actually trigger it. If you cannot trigger it, it is refuted (or downgrade it to a theoretical 'minor').
- If it claims a source-level divergence from the canonical earcut algorithm, decide whether it could EVER change the
  emitted index sequence for ANY input, not just the gear fixture. If it cannot, say so and mark it not real.
- If it is a requirements/packaging claim, check the filesystem yourself.
Set real=true ONLY if it survives. Give the exact commands you ran and their real output in "evidence".

#!/bin/bash
# Differential test harness: compares /output/test11 against the reference C++
# binary byte-for-byte (stdout, stderr and exit status) for a list of argv[1]
# values supplied on stdin (one raw value per line; the literal token
# @@NOARG@@ means "invoke with no arguments").
REF=/workspace/dataset/test11_executable
RUST=/output/test11
fail=0
count=0
while IFS= read -r arg; do
  count=$((count+1))
  if [ "$arg" == "@@NOARG@@" ]; then
    "$REF"  >/tmp/ref.out 2>/tmp/ref.err; rs=$?
    "$RUST" >/tmp/rus.out 2>/tmp/rus.err; ns=$?
  else
    "$REF"  "$arg" >/tmp/ref.out 2>/tmp/ref.err; rs=$?
    "$RUST" "$arg" >/tmp/rus.out 2>/tmp/rus.err; ns=$?
  fi
  if ! cmp -s /tmp/ref.out /tmp/rus.out; then
    echo "STDOUT MISMATCH for arg=[$arg]"
    echo "  ref bytes: $(wc -c </tmp/ref.out)  rust bytes: $(wc -c </tmp/rus.out)"
    cmp /tmp/ref.out /tmp/rus.out | head -2
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
  if [ "$rs" != "$ns" ]; then
    echo "EXIT MISMATCH for arg=[$arg]: ref=$rs rust=$ns"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
done
echo "checked=$count failures=$fail"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]
